body:
- **Myth vs. fact table** for the writer:
  - "Buffett got rich from cigar butts" — false in dollars. Cigar butts built his seed capital. The wealth came from leveraged, float-funded quality compounding, mostly after age 50–65.
  - "Buffett's alpha is magic or luck" — neither, per AQR. It is factor exposure, cheap leverage and survival, and he spotted those factors decades before academics did.
  - "Buffett bet 40% on Amex" — plausible and widely reported, but not verified here against the primary letter.
  - "Lynch: buy what you know" — oversimplified. He meant "know what you own," backed by 200+ visits a year.
  - "Most Magellan investors lost money" — no study exists. Fidelity denied it. What happened is a dollar-weighted shortfall.
- **The most transferable lesson for a small investor:** a small capital base is a real edge in obscure securities if paired with Buffett- or Lynch-level reading and visit volume, plus a structure that never forces selling, meaning no margin calls and no redemptions.

data.section: Inferences

title: buffett_lynch › Inferences

body: Time and starting capital dominate the rate of return. About 99% of Buffett's fortune came after age 65. High returns for a few years build very little. ₹1 lakh compounding at 30% for a decade is about ₹14 lakh, which is not generational wealth. Ordinary people who got rich through markets (Ronald Read, Grace Groner) did it through decades of patience, frugality, and reinvested dividends, not brilliance.

`case_study:ilfs-2018` | 2018-09-04 | tickers: ILFSENGG, ILFSTRANS | confidence: verified

Infrastructure Leasing & Financial Services (owned by LIC, SBI, ORIX, ADIA, HDFC) had ~Rs 91,000 cr group debt across 300+ subsidiaries by Mar 2018 and AAA ratings on some paper until early Aug 2018. First default came at subsidiary IL&FS Transportation (ITNL) in Jun 2018 (~Rs 450 cr ICDs/CP); ICRA cut AAA to AA+ in Jul; the parent defaulted on a Rs 1,000 cr SIDBI loan on 4 Sep 2018; within days ratings went AAA -> D. The government superseded the board on 1 Oct 2018 (Uday Kotak-led). Listed subsidiaries ITNL and IL&FS Engineering fell >90%. The default froze India's CP market and triggered the NBFC crisis (DHFL, Reliance Capital, Altico). Visible flags: (1) consolidated interest coverage near/below 1x -- operating cash flow did not cover interest; (2) long-gestation road/power projects funded with short debt and constant refinancing; (3) 300+ subsidiaries/cross-guarantees made consolidated leverage opaque; (4) ratings leaned on 'parentage' (LIC/SBI) not standalone cash; (5) listed ITNL showed rising debt, receivables from government authorities and claims-based 'income'. Lesson: AAA is not a cash-flow test; a holding structure that needs perpetual refinancing fails the day markets close; rating agency downgrades are lagging.

**Lesson:** Compute interest cover and refinancing needs yourself; parentage-based ratings lag
**Spotted early by:** few; ICRA July 2018 note was late
**Links:** illustrates -> `insight:avoid-ruin`, illustrates -> `insight:lender-blowup-signals`
**Sources:** <https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/how-il-fs-tripped-118092501323_1.html> ; <https://www.business-standard.com/amp/article/companies/il-fs-default-did-rating-agencies-failure-to-connect-dots-lead-to-crisis-118092800364_1.html> ; <https://www.bloombergquint.com/business/the-rise-and-stumble-of-ilfs> ; <https://eparlib.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/801273/1/AU886.pdf>

`case_study:asml-2012-2024` · tickers US-ASML · confidence: verified

July-Sept 2012: Intel, TSMC and Samsung took a combined 23% stake in ASML for €3.85bn and committed €1.38bn to EUV and 450mm R&D (customer co-investment program; Intel ~15%, TSMC 5%, Samsung 3%). ASML also bought Cymer (light source) in 2012-13. EUV took until ~2017-19 to reach volume production; ASML is the only supplier, enabling 7nm and below. ADR ~$49 (July 2012, Intel investment date) -> ~$172 (Oct 2018, +350%) -> peak ~$1,100 (July 2024) [unverified] ≈ 22x plus dividends. Split [approx]: EPS ~€2.6 (2012) -> ~€19 (2024) ≈ 7x; P/E ~20x -> ~40x ≈ 2x. Drawdowns: ~-59% (Nov 2021-Oct 2022) and ~-45-50% (July 2024-2025) on China export curbs and order softness [unverified]. EARLY SIGNAL visible in 2012: the three largest chipmakers paying billions for equity to make sure EUV got built — customers voting with capital for a single-source chokepoint. Samsung's retained stake reportedly grew ~17x. Who caught it: the customers themselves (TSMC sold out 2015, Intel/Samsung trimmed from 2016 — leaving most of the gain on the table). LESSON: when customers co-fund a supplier's monopoly technology, the moat is being built in public; the payoff took 5-7 years of technical risk and the stock stays cyclical (-50% swings) even as a monopoly.

- **Start → end:** ~$49 ADR (Jul 2012) → ~$1,100 (Jul 2024) [unverified] (~22x)
- **EPS vs rerating:** EPS ~7x, P/E ~2x [approx]
- **Max drawdown:** ~-59% (2021-22)
- **Early signal:** Intel/TSMC/Samsung €3.85bn equity co-investment for EUV
- **Who caught it:** customers (Intel, TSMC, Samsung) — most sold early
- **Ended/stalled:** 2024 peak; China curbs/cycle
- **Lesson:** customer co-investment = public moat signal; monopolies stay cyclical
- **Sources:** [1](https://asml.com/en/news/press-releases/2012/asml-issues-shares-to-tsmc-in-connection-with-customer-co-investment-program) · [2](https://optics.org/news/asml-shareholders-back-lithography-investment) · [3](https://www.eetasia.com/18101601-intel-reduces-asml-stake) · [4](https://www.sammobile.com/news/brilliant-investment-earned-samsung-a-staggering-17x-return/)

body:
- **The second 75k t block has had five dates.** In order: Mar-26 (said Jul-25); "partly before March, rest Q1" (Jan-26); June-26 (Apr-26); "H2" and "end of Q2" (Aug-26); "end of Q3 or early Q4" (Oct-26). Each new date was given **without acknowledging the previous one**. The only explanation offered was "minor delays", in Jan-26, and only when asked.
- **600k t moved from FY28 to FY29.** The Oct-26 opening remarks gave FY29 with no mention that the target had been FY28-end since Jul-25.
- **FY26 revenue "25% plus", raised in Jul-25 and re-affirmed in Nov-25:** delivered +20%. The cut first appeared in the Jan-26 presentation. When an analyst asked, management said: "the 25% is -- was our aspirational growth."
- **FY26 order inflow:** guided INR 6,500-7,000 cr in Jul-25, quietly re-stated as "INR 6,000 cr plus" in Nov-25. Actual: INR 5,678 cr.
- **Export order inflow:** promised to "double to INR 1,500 crores this year for sure" in FY26. Actual: about INR 730 cr. That figure is implied by the Q1FY27 statement that ~INR 1,100 cr would be "+50% over last year".
- **Polymer (pipes):**
  - growth guided at 20-25% (Oct-24), then 25-30% (Apr-25); actual FY25 roughly flat, FY26 +11%;
  - the INR 1,000 cr target moved from "2-3 years" (Jul-24) to "if not next year, the year after" (Nov-25), then lost its date entirely (Apr-26);
  - the double-digit margin moved from "next year" (Jul-25) to "long term" four months later (Nov-25).
- **Infra segment FY26:** guided +20-25%; derived actual about +2% (≈ INR 687 cr vs 674 cr).
- **"No further capital raising beyond the rights issue; internal accruals will be strong enough" (Jul-24):**
  - three months later the Board took an enabling resolution for ~INR 600 cr;
  - in 2026 the company raised INR 433.5 cr by preferential issue;
  - free cash flow was negative in both FY25 (−83 cr) and FY26 (−88 cr).
- **FY25 finance cost below 4.5% of revenue:** actual 4.6-4.8%. The miss was never acknowledged. Later calls described the FY25 base as 4.7% (Nov-25) and then 4.8% (Jan-26), which makes the FY26 improvement look larger.
- **Silently dropped:** "25% CAGR over three years, INR 10,000 cr revenue by ~FY29" (Oct-24 interview claim, affirmed on the call). It was never repeated in the eight later calls; in Feb-25 management "would refrain from putting any specific guidance numbers". It is still arithmetically reachable, since FY24 to FY27e is about a 25% CAGR if FY27 delivers +15%.

data.section: Caveats

title: solvency_flags_india › Caveats

body:
Federal Bank dry run (stages 2→6, practice, no verdict): 19 gaps found, 14 fixed. Biggest: range parsing read
"18–20%" as −20% (affected SKIPPER pending targets; re-scored: no status changed, goalpost moves 12→10);
NIM scored as cost/revenue; bank transcripts on NSE are cover letters only; no bank valuation mode (added P/B–ROE).
Good-but-misleading rows outnumbered bad-but-benign 10 to 6: retail loan growth 18% → 4% ex special FCNR window;
GNPA "10-year low" helped by write-offs > slippages; PCR 87% → 76.6% ex one-off; ROE 13.6% → ~10% after warrants.
**Rule:** run a full dry run whenever a new sector type enters the pipeline; for banks always strip special
windows, write-offs and one-offs before trusting headline asset-quality and growth numbers.
